ideas.title: Tied together
ideas.critique: Nothing on the island has ever connected bodies physically. A verlet rope that wraps round trunks and fights ten creatures' own goals is new physics that makes stories nobody wrote, and Lumi pulling on it makes it playable. The risk is the plain version, where springs just drag everyone into one jittering clump; it only holds up if the wraps, catapults and tangles really happen and the motion stays clean under the rope forces.

ideas.title: Jelly day, for real
ideas.critique: This is round 2's Jelly day again. It is still another 'the whole ground does something to everyone' day after the seesaw and the dunes. The part that's new is the feedback loop, where a landing makes new rings and the chain of bounces runs on by itself; stomping to launch a friend far away is worth coming back to, but only if the wave equation really drives it and no hidden timer does.

ideas.title: Lumi turns magnetic
ideas.critique: Props sticking to a body and making it heavier is a new way things move, and a clump of metal is good path tracer material. But 'touches the TV, gets magnetic, shakes it all off' is a gag with an obvious arc, and the friend in a crown is a scripted beat. It is fun to waddle around once; whether it lasts depends on the stuck pile behaving physically and not just as parented meshes.

ideas.title: Two heads
ideas.critique: One body pulled by two goals is a small version of the rope idea with one link instead of many, and a fused hybrid creature echoes the breeding pen's mixed bodies. Ending on a sneeze is a scripted punchline, and a single walk across the meadow is a film you watch once. The zigzag tug is honest emergent motion, but it is thin.
